subproblem.title: Continuity on a Simon submanifold can be checked in charts
subproblem.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, r ∈ ℕ∞, let M ⊆ ℝᴺ be an n-dimensional C^r Simon submanifold (Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := ℝⁿ) r M), let X be a topological space and F : ℝᴺ → X. Suppose that for every chart (V, W, ψ) of M of class r (Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ, ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ) the map x ↦ F(ψ(x)) is continuous on V. Then F is continuous on M.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (r : ℕ∞) (M : Set (Rn N)) (X : Type) [TopologicalSpace X] (F : Rn N → X), Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Rn n) r M → (∀ (V : Set (Rn n)) (W : Set (Rn N)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), Chapter02.IsSimonLocalRepresentation r M V W ψ → ContinuousOn (fun x ↦ F (ψ x)) V) → ContinuousOn F M
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 5, second half ("ψ restricts to a homeomorphism of V onto W ∩ M; hence H = h ∘ (ψ|_V)⁻¹ is continuous on W ∩ M. Given y₀ ∈ M, choose such a chart with y₀ ∈ W; ... W is a neighbourhood of y₀, so H is continuous within M at y₀"), stated for an arbitrary F. The homeomorphism property comes from the relative properness of the chart. SimonGMT proves it as IsSimonLocalRepresentation.isEmbedding_chartMap / exists_open_image_eq_inter (Simon 4.2), but their module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.SubmanifoldTopology is not in the frozen import closure and a leaf may not add imports, so the needed instance of that argument is carried out directly from the chart fields.
1. Fix y₀ ∈ M. We show that F is continuous within M at y₀: for every neighbourhood O of F(y₀) in X, F⁻¹(O) is a neighbourhood of y₀ within M.
2. (A chart through y₀.) By the definition of IsSimonSubmanifold r M there is a chart (V, W, ψ) of class r with y₀ ∈ W. Since ψ(V) = W ∩ M ∋ y₀, there is x₀ ∈ V with ψ(x₀) = y₀.
3. (Continuity in the chart.) By hypothesis x ↦ F(ψ(x)) is continuous on V; as V is open and x₀ ∈ V, it is continuous at x₀ (ContinuousWithinAt.continuousAt). Hence there is an open U₀ ⊆ ℝⁿ with x₀ ∈ U₀ and F(ψ(x)) ∈ O for all x ∈ U₀.
4. (A compact piece of the chart.) W is open and y₀ ∈ W, so there is ε > 0 with Q := closedBall(y₀, ε) ⊆ W. Q is compact, so by the relative properness of the chart (isCompact_source_inter_preimage) K := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) is compact. Then K \ U₀ = K ∩ U₀ᶜ is compact (a closed subset of a compact set, as U₀ is open), and ψ is continuous on V ⊇ K \ U₀ (ψ is C^r on V), so C := ψ(K \ U₀) is compact, hence closed in ℝᴺ.
5. (y₀ ∉ C.) If y₀ = ψ(x) with x ∈ K \ U₀ ⊆ V, then ψ(x) = ψ(x₀) with x, x₀ ∈ V, so x = x₀ by injectivity of ψ on V; but x₀ ∈ U₀ while x ∉ U₀, a contradiction.
6. (F maps a neighbourhood of y₀ in M into O.) W₀ := ball(y₀, ε) \ C is open (an open set minus a closed set) and contains y₀ (steps 4–5). Let z ∈ W₀ ∩ M. Then z ∈ ball(y₀, ε) ⊆ Q ⊆ W, so z ∈ W ∩ M = ψ(V): z = ψ(x) with x ∈ V, and x ∈ K because ψ(x) = z ∈ Q. If x ∉ U₀, then x ∈ K \ U₀ and z = ψ(x) ∈ C, contradicting z ∈ W₀; hence x ∈ U₀ and F(z) = F(ψ(x)) ∈ O by step 3. Thus W₀ ∩ M ⊆ F⁻¹(O).
7. Since W₀ is open and y₀ ∈ W₀, the set W₀ ∩ M, and hence F⁻¹(O) ⊇ W₀ ∩ M, is a neighbourhood of y₀ within M (mem_nhdsWithin). As O and y₀ ∈ M were arbitrary, F is continuous on M. ∎

Only the frozen imports are needed: the chart fields are exposed by Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.Submanifold (image_eq, isOpen_source, isOpen_target, contDiffOn, injOn, isCompact_source_inter_preimage). With Q = closedBall(y₀, ε) ⊆ W, relative properness makes K = V ∩ ψ⁻¹(Q) compact, so C = ψ(K \ U₀) is compact and closed.
Injectivity of ψ on V gives y₀ ∉ C, so W₀ = ball(y₀, ε) \ C is an open neighbourhood of y₀.
Every z ∈ W₀ ∩ M is ψ(x) with x ∈ K ∩ U₀, so F(z) ∈ O; hence F⁻¹(O) ∈ 𝓝[M] y₀ and F is continuous on M.

subproblem.title: The Gram operator A*A of an injective linear map is invertible
subproblem.statement: For all n, N ∈ ℕ and every continuous linear map A : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ (ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) that is injective, the Gram operator G := A* ∘ A : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ (A* = ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A, the Hilbert adjoint) is a unit of the ring ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ, whose multiplication is composition; i.e. G has a two-sided inverse that is a continuous linear map.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn N), Function.Injective A → IsUnit (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A ∘L A)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 4 ("G(x) := A(x)*A(x) (symmetric, positive definite, invertible)") and step 5 ("inversion is continuous on invertible operators"); this child isolates the invertibility of the Gram operator, which both the chart formula for H (sibling mean_curvature_gram) and its continuity (sibling mean_curvature_chart_continuous) use.
Setting. A : ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝᴺ is injective, A* := ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A : ℝᴺ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ is characterised by ⟨u, A* w⟩ = ⟨A u, w⟩ for u ∈ ℝⁿ, w ∈ ℝᴺ (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right), and G := A* ∘L A. In the monoid ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ the product is composition, (S * T) v = S (T v), and 1 = id.
1. (Trivial kernel.) Let w ∈ ℝⁿ with G w = 0. Then ‖A w‖² = ⟨A w, A w⟩ = ⟨w, A*(A w)⟩ = ⟨w, G w⟩ = ⟨w, 0⟩ = 0, so A w = 0 = A 0 (inner_self_eq_zero), and injectivity of A gives w = 0.
2. (Injectivity.) If G u = G v, then G(u − v) = G u − G v = 0 by linearity, so u − v = 0 by step 1, i.e. u = v. Thus G is injective.
3. (Bijectivity.) ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional and G is an injective linear endomorphism of it, hence G is surjective (rank–nullity); Mathlib packages this as the linear automorphism LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo G.toLinearMap (step 2), whose underlying function is G. A linear map between finite-dimensional normed spaces is continuous, so this automorphism and its inverse are continuous: it upgrades to a continuous linear automorphism e : ℝⁿ ≃L[ℝ] ℝⁿ (LinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearEquiv) with e v = G v for every v.
4. (Unit.) A continuous linear automorphism e of ℝⁿ gives the unit e.toUnit of ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ (ContinuousLinearEquiv.toUnit), whose underlying continuous linear map is e (as a map). By step 3 this underlying map equals G (ext: both send v to G v). Hence IsUnit G, i.e. IsUnit (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint A ∘L A). ∎
Formalization note. No imports beyond GMT.Ch02.Submission are needed. The multiplication on ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ used by IsUnit is composition ((G * H) v = G (H v) holds by rfl), so the unit is the operator inverse, not a pointwise one. A 20-line Lean proof following steps 1–4 (ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_inner_right, inner_self_eq_zero, LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo, LinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearEquiv, ContinuousLinearEquiv.toUnit) compiled warning-free against the frozen contract with only `import GMT.Ch02.Submission` and axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
proof_key_steps: G w = 0 implies ‖A w‖² = ⟨w, A*A w⟩ = 0, so A w = 0 and w = 0; hence G is injective.
An injective endomorphism of the finite-dimensional ℝⁿ is a linear automorphism, automatically continuous (ofInjectiveEndo, toContinuousLinearEquiv).
The continuous linear automorphism yields a unit of ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝⁿ (toUnit) whose value is G, so IsUnit (A* ∘L A).

audit.reason: The adjoint identity proves trivial kernel; finite dimensionality supplies a continuous linear automorphism and its associated unit. The inferred ring multiplication is demonstrably composition. The proof establishes the exact type, including dimension zero.

subproblem.title: Symmetry of the second derivative of a C² map (Schwarz)
subproblem.statement: For all n, N ∈ ℕ, every f : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ (ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) and every x ∈ ℝⁿ such that f is C² at x (ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x), the second derivative L := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x is symmetric: L a b = L b a for all a, b ∈ ℝⁿ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (f : Rn n → Rn N) (x : Rn n), ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x → ∀ a b : Rn n, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x a b = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x b a
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof step 1 ("ψ is C² on the open set V ∋ x, so ContDiffAt ℝ 2 ψ x and its second derivative at x is symmetric: S_x(a, b) = S_x(b, a) (ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt, with minSmoothness ℝ 2 = 2)"). The cited Mathlib lemma lives in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.FDeriv.Symmetric, which is not in the import closure of the frozen contract, and a leaf may not add imports; this child therefore supplies the classical proof of Schwarz's theorem from the mean value inequality and the chain rule, which are available.
Notation. Df(y) := fderiv ℝ f y ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) and L := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) x ∈ L(ℝⁿ, L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ)); L is linear in each argument, so L(ta)(tb) = t² L a b. Norms of linear maps are operator norms.
1. (Regularity.) Since f is C² at x and 2 ≠ ∞, f is C² on a neighbourhood of x (ContDiffAt.eventually), in particular differentiable at every point of a neighbourhood of x. Moreover y ↦ Df(y) is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.fderiv_right with 1 + 1 ≤ 2), hence differentiable at x: Df has Fréchet derivative L at x.
